canonical.title: Dual-boot Linux next to Windows in 2026 without wrecking the Windows install

parent.title: Testing the waters: a staged, reversible path from a Windows dev workstation to Linux

siblings.title: The staged ladder: what each rung of a Windows→Linux move actually proves
siblings.summary: A rung-by-rung ladder from WSL2 to full switch, with what each rung proves, what it structurally hides, the go/no-go signal, and the cost of retreating.

siblings.title: WSL2 as rung zero — what it proves, and the exact wall it hits
siblings.summary: WSL2 retires every userland risk in a Linux migration and none of the machine-ownership risks; here is where the line falls in 2026.

siblings.title: Dropbox on Linux and shared folders: what actually works in 2026
siblings.summary: The official Linux client now supports btrfs/zfs/xfs, but you cannot share one Dropbox folder between a Windows and a Linux install, and code repos do not belong in Dropbox at all.

siblings.title: Trial hardware and VM paths for evaluating Linux before you commit (2026)
siblings.summary: Live USB first (€10, 15 minutes, proves your actual hardware), then a full install on an external NVMe SSD (€90–150) — everything else is a detour.

siblings.title: Living in both OSes: running Windows and Linux for months without your setup rotting
siblings.summary: One source of truth per asset class, replicated by a tool that knows the OS difference — never a shared partition and never two hand-edited copies.

siblings.title: Exit criteria and the blocker inventory: decide the Linux switch on evidence, not vibes
siblings.summary: A fill-in blocker inventory plus tickable go/no-go criteria and a pre-committed rollback date for a Windows-to-Linux workstation trial.

sources.title: ArchWiki — Dual boot with Windows
sources.claim: Canonical reference for Fast Startup/hibernation corruption, one-ESP-per-drive, Windows Setup's 100 MiB ESP, BitLocker-on-by-default in Windows 11, the Secure Boot/Windows Hello trade-off, and bcdboot ESP recovery.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn — Cannot boot Windows on the primary hard disk (UEFI)
sources.claim: Microsoft documents that a second ESP created on a second disk can make the original Windows install unbootable; the only supported multi-install layout uses a single ESP.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn — BitLocker FAQ
sources.claim: Suspend wraps the volume master key with a clear key and reseals on resume; a non-Windows OS booting before Windows prevents BitLocker binding to PCR 7; recovery is impossible without the key.

sources.title: Microsoft Support — Windows Secure Boot certificate expiration and CA updates
sources.claim: Exact expiry dates and 2023 replacements for Microsoft KEK CA 2011, Microsoft UEFI CA 2011 and Windows Production PCA 2011, and confirmation that un-updated devices keep booting.

sources.title: Linux Mint Forums — separate drives for dual boot
sources.claim: Community consensus that separate physical drives avoid OEM recovery partitions and vendor RAID/RST setups and keep the Linux install portable.

sources.title: Tom's Guide Forums — Dual booting two hard drives
sources.claim: Practitioner advice to physically disconnect the Windows drive while installing Linux so each OS is fully self-contained on its own disk.

sources.title: ArchWiki — EFI system partition
sources.claim: Recommended ESP sizing and that a separate ESP per OS is the preferred hibernation mitigation, supported when the ESPs reside on physically different disks.

sources.title: MakeUseOf — the Windows feature that wrecks Linux files
sources.claim: Fast Startup leaves NTFS volumes in a suspended, hibernation-flagged state so Linux writes can corrupt them; disabling it is the only root-cause fix.

sources.title: Super User — Hibernating and booting into another OS
sources.claim: Original explanation of why hibernating one OS and mounting its filesystems from another corrupts them.

sources.title: Winhelponline — You cannot shrink a volume beyond the point…
sources.claim: Windows Disk Management can only shrink up to the last unmovable file; pagefile.sys, hiberfil.sys and System Volume Information are the usual blockers.

sources.title: MSPoweruser — Windows 11 24H2 enables default BitLocker encryption on more devices
sources.claim: Windows 11 24H2 enables automatic device encryption on clean installs signed in with a Microsoft or work account, across all editions including Home.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn — BitLocker recovery overview
sources.claim: Full list of BitLocker recovery triggers, the recommendation to suspend for planned changes, and that manually-started Windows RE needs the recovery key.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn — Prompted for BitLocker recovery key after UEFI/TPM firmware updates
sources.claim: Vendor UEFI and TPM firmware updates on their own can prompt for the BitLocker recovery key.

sources.title: sbctl wiki — Linux/Windows dual boot with BitLocker
sources.claim: Modern BitLocker seals to TPM2 and needs Secure Boot enabled to unseal; without it you get the recovery prompt on every Windows boot.

sources.title: ArchWiki — systemd-cryptenroll
sources.claim: TPM-sealed LUKS unlock bound to PCR 7 requires Secure Boot active in user mode, making it break on the same Secure Boot changes that break BitLocker.

sources.title: Red Hat — Expiration of Secure Boot signing certificates in 2026
sources.claim: Existing shims keep booting after the 2026 expiry; distros ship dual-signed shims; do not remove the 2011 certificate after enrolling the 2023 one.

sources.title: Ubuntu documentation — Secure Boot
sources.claim: Ubuntu ships a Microsoft-signed shim and Canonical-signed GRUB, generates machine-specific MOKs, automates DKMS module signing, and refuses to load unsigned modules.

sources.title: BleepingComputer — Microsoft confirms August updates break Linux boot in dual-boot systems
sources.claim: The August 2024 Windows security update applied an SBAT revocation that broke Linux boot on dual-boot machines.

sources.title: ArchWiki — Unified Extensible Firmware Interface
sources.claim: Documented causes and workarounds for Windows taking over the UEFI boot order, including firmware overriding efibootmgr and the overwritten fallback path.

sources.title: ArchWiki — systemd-boot
sources.claim: systemd-boot is a minimal UEFI-only boot manager that auto-detects Windows Boot Manager without manual loader configuration.

sources.title: CachyOS wiki — Boot managers
sources.claim: On firmware that is not fully UEFI-spec-compliant, systemd-boot or Limine are recommended over GRUB and rEFInd.

sources.title: Arch Linux Forums — efibootmgr boot order does not persist
sources.claim: Real report that efibootmgr boot-order changes do not persist because Windows puts itself back on top at the next startup.

sources.title: Ubuntu Community Help — Boot-Repair
sources.claim: Boot-Repair reinstalls GRUB and restores access to previously installed operating systems, and produces a Boot-Info report first.

sources.title: It's FOSS — Uninstall Ubuntu from a Windows dual boot
sources.claim: Procedure for removing Linux from a dual boot: delete the Linux volumes, extend the Windows partition, remove the leftover EFI directory and firmware boot entry.

sources.title: ArchWiki — NTFS
sources.claim: Linux has two in-tree read-write NTFS drivers in 2026; neither is objectively better; ntfs3 refuses dirty volumes without force; windows_names enforces Windows filename rules.

sources.title: The Register — Linux 7.1 gains a new NTFS driver
sources.claim: Linux 7.1 gained an optional new NTFS driver (formerly NTFSPLUS) alongside ntfs3.

sources.title: Dedoimedo — Linux NTFS driver reliability
sources.claim: Independent long-term testing recommends the slower userspace ntfs-3g over ntfs3 for reliability with large data sets.

sources.title: subzerodays — Creating a git repo on NTFS in Linux
sources.claim: git init/clone fails on an NTFS mount because git chmods files inside .git/ and the driver returns an error.

sources.title: botmonster — Dual-boot Linux/Windows shared storage
sources.claim: A shared exFAT/NTFS partition cannot store Linux permissions, symlinks or POSIX attributes; keep repos on the native filesystem of each OS.

sources.title: Paragon Software — NTFS3 driver FAQ
sources.claim: Vendor reference for the ntfs3 kernel driver and its mount options; shipped in the kernel since 5.15.
